newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF clinches Ecuador deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF clinches Ecuador deal.

text.p: Argentine oil firm YPF SA said Wednesday it had successfully concluded negotiations with the Ecuadorean government on terms of a new joint-venture contract for its Block 16 operation in Ecuador.

The new contract "complies with the double objective of protecting both the interests of the government and of the people of Ecuador as well as those of the companies which are members of the Block 16 consortium," YPF said, without giving details of the new agreement.

Ecuador's government last August banned YPF's U.S.-based subsidiary Maxus Energy Corp from continuing its oil operations in the country until the firm reached an agreement to share output at Block 16 with state-owned Petroecuador.

YPF added, "YPF Ecuador Inc and YPF SA are happy that the talks have reached a happy conclusion and at the same time express their wish to continue working and investing in Ecuador within the framework of respect for the law."

Ecuadorean law states that foreign oil companies should in principle pay 12.5 percent of production to the state. YPF was the only firm operating in the country without a production-sharing deal under the regulation.
